title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: GAIL'S GOLF CLUBS
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Gail Pemberton, an office manager at a cotton gin in Lubbock, Texas.
For thirty years, her husband Dale golfed every Saturday while Gail stayed home.
Then Dale retired, and said he'd now play every single day.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE GARAGE SALE
segments.quote: I want to do it because I want to do it.
segments.author: Amelia Earhart
lines: At a garage sale, Gail found pink golf clubs for twenty dollars.
Her sister laughed. Gail, you're fifty-eight. You don't even like grass.
Gail thought of Amelia Earhart's note before her last flight:
I want to do it because I want to do it.
She paid the twenty dollars, and didn't tell Dale.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE FIRST SWING
segments.quote: Golf is deceptively simple and endlessly complicated.
segments.author: Arnold Palmer
lines: At the range, a teenage coach named Jace watched her swing nine times.
Eight times she hit air. Once she hit the bucket.
Jace shrugged and quoted the great Arnold Palmer:
Golf is deceptively simple and endlessly complicated.
So Gail stopped swinging for the moon. She just tapped it. It rolled. She cheered like it was a hole in one.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE BUTTERFLIES
segments.quote: The least thing upset him on the links. He missed short putts because of the uproar of the butterflies in the adjoining meadows.
segments.author: P. G. Wodehouse
lines: Soon Gail had an excuse for every bad shot. The wind. A bird with an attitude.
Then she read a golf story by the English humorist P. G. Wodehouse:
The least thing upset him on the links. He missed short putts because of the uproar of the butterflies in the adjoining meadows.
Gail laughed so hard she had to sit down. No more excuses. Just the next shot.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: NOBODY SAW
segments.quote: You might as well praise me for not robbing a bank.
segments.author: Bobby Jones
lines: In her first ladies' tournament, her ball moved when she touched it. Nobody saw.
She remembered Bobby Jones, who once called that penalty on himself and lost the U.S. Open. Praised for it, he said,
You might as well praise me for not robbing a bank.
Gail counted the stroke. She finished last, and slept like a baby.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: DALE FINDS OUT
segments.quote: Eighteen holes of match play will teach you more about your foe than eighteen years of dealing with him across a desk.
segments.author: Grantland Rice
lines: Then Dale found the pink clubs in the trunk, and challenged her to a match.
Gail remembered the sportswriter Grantland Rice:
Eighteen holes of match play will teach you more about your foe than eighteen years of dealing with him across a desk.
That day she learned Dale hums when he's nervous, and calls his ball Sweetheart.
He has never once called Gail Sweetheart.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE FLOWERS
segments.quote: You're only here for a short visit. Don't hurry. Don't worry. And be sure to smell the flowers along the way.
segments.author: Walter Hagen
lines: Gail won by one stroke. Dale sulked for a mile.
Then she quoted the old champion Walter Hagen:
You're only here for a short visit. Don't hurry. Don't worry. And be sure to smell the flowers along the way.
Now they play every Saturday together, and stop for pie on the way home.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Start anyway. Keep it simple. No excuses. Play fair. Pay attention. Smell the flowers.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Start anyway. Keep it simple. Drop the excuses. Play fair. Pay attention. Smell the flowers.
I tried golf once. They asked me to keep score. I ran out of pencil.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
